title: A reason to read, kept in view
statement: Before students start, give them one purpose for reading that points at the evidence the later task will use, and keep the lesson's question and steps on screen.
detail: A review of grade-3 showcase lessons found a lesson with no stated purpose for reading and asked for a reason to read before the children start; it also found the modelling steps and the live question scrolling away, so the child lost the thread, and asked that both stay visible with one thing surfaced at a time. The Year 9 lesson design specification gives every lesson one learning question that every phase builds toward, annotated and pinned to the top of every screen. The purpose must not teach the later task's answer, and the current steps stay on screen while students work.

evidence.quote: Children need a reason to read before they start
The steps and live question must remain visible, and the model should surface one thing at a time
